transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-04-16
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (CTO), Eliot Park (ML Eng), Samir Khan (Infra), Sam (Product)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, I'm the AE on the account, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Marta (Customer CTO): Good, thanks. We got about 45 minutes. Want to focus on migration questions — mostly compatibility and performance.
[00:12] Jordan: Perfect. Quick agenda: current stack, goals for migration, compatibility concerns with OpenAI APIs, pilot/benchmark plan, and security/compliance. Priya will jump into technicals. Sound ok?
[00:20] Marta: Yep.
[00:25] Priya (Redwood SE): Cool. Eliot, can you kick off with current infra and where you call OpenAI now?
[00:30] Eliot (ML Eng): Sure, we use OpenAI for chat completions and embeddings. Mostly gpt-4 style for summaries and a smaller model for retrieval-augmented generation. Traffic is bursty: peak 300rps, avg 30. Latency budget is 200-300ms p95 for chat. Cost is getting out of control.
[00:45] Priya: Thanks. Are you currently on API a single key per environment? Any compliance reqs?
[00:50] Samir (Infra): We have SSO, SAML, and envelope KMS for secrets. We need SOC2 and VPC peering for any private deployment.
[00:57] Jordan: Totally. One of the big asks we see is keeping eval parity. How sensitive are you to exact output changes coming from different model runtimes?
[01:05] Marta: Very. Our product is clinical summaries so hallucination/reliability matters. If responses change vs OpenAI in ways that affect downstream scores, that's a problem.
[01:15] Priya: Understood. On parity there are two angles: model weights and runtime. If you want bit-for-bit parity you need the same model weights and same sampling seeds — usually not possible for closed models. For open models, we've seen good parity moving from hosted inference to Dedicated, but we recommend an eval suite.
[01:33] Eliot: We're worried about vLLM/TGI differences too — some of our internal infra uses vLLM for cost saving, but outputs drift. Can Redwood run the same model variants we use?
[01:42] Priya: Redwood supports a catalog of open models and can run custom checkpoints in Dedicated/Private in many cases; runtime differences like KV cache behavior and attention optimizations can slightly change tokenization/outputs. We provide a recommended quantization profile and an eval harness to measure BLEU/ROUGE/clinical-specific metrics.
[02:02] Jordan: Also routing and fallback — we can fall back to a hosted variant if a private capacity issue occurs. That helps maintain availability during pilot.
[02:10] Sam (Product): What's the lift to switch from OpenAI calls to Redwood? Do we need to change code?
[02:16] Priya: Minimal. We expose an OpenAI-compatible REST/SDK interface for generation and embeddings. Most customers change the base URL and update keys; for specific params there might be small name diffs but we keep them very compatible.
[02:31] Marta: Ok, but what about function calling and structured outputs? We rely on function calls heavily.
[02:36] Priya: We support streaming, function/tool calling, and structured output. Function schema handling is compatible in our SDKs. We will run your function-calling prompt set in the benchmark.
[02:46] Eliot: For perf, do you have numbers for p95 latency on chat? Our p95 target 200-300ms.
[02:51] Priya: On Dedicated we typically hit 100-250ms p95 for 1-2k token context on Ampere/GR8 type nodes — depends on batch sizing and KV cache warmness. We'll size the cluster based on your traffic profile — we have autoscaling and burst capacity.
[03:12] Samir: Network egress is a concern. If we go Private in our VPC, does data leave our VPC? How do you handle KMS?
[03:18] Jordan: For Private deployments, the control plane can be customer-managed; for VPC we support private connectivity and your KMS/HSM. We can integrate with your envelope KMS so keys stay with you.
[03:28] Marta: SOC2 and audit logs — we need retention and searchable logs for audits.
[03:33] Priya: We provide audit logs, per-token cost traces, and integrations for SIEM. SOC2 reports and compliance pack are something Jordan will share.
[03:41] Eliot: Back to eval parity — you mentioned quantization. We're using int8 in vLLM — does Redwood's quantization change outputs?
[03:48] Priya: Quantization can slightly affect outputs. We provide quantization profiles tuned for quality preservation. For high-fidelity needs we recommend float16 or low-loss int8 plus running your eval set to measure drift.
[04:00] Jordan: Typical approach: run your eval set against OpenAI (prod baseline), then run on Redwood hosted/Dedicated with same prompts and measure delta. We'll help with that pipeline.
[04:08] Marta: Good. How about model variants? We sometimes need a smaller cheaper worker model for some flows. Can you route based on policy?
[04:15] Priya: Yes — smart routing by policy (latency, cost, region, customer tier). You can set a fallback model or prune expensive calls to cheaper variants.
[04:25] Eliot: Pilot — what's a realistic pilot? We want to test parity on 2-3 flows and stress to 300rps peak for an hour.
[04:33] Jordan: We recommend a 2-week pilot: week 1 dry-run (eval parity, deterministic prompts), week 2 traffic soak and latency testing with a mirrored subset. We'll size a small Dedicated pool to your spec.
[04:44] Samir: Cost model for Dedicated — committed vs burst? We'd like predictable monthly.
[04:49] Jordan: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits. There's burst capacity options billed separately. We can show per-token modeled costs vs OpenAI.
[04:59] Marta: What about open-source runtimes like TGI? Our infra team has some experience.
[05:04] Priya: We can run models on top of TGI/vLLM in Private deployments but we manage the runtime differences. For Dedicated we control the runtime optimizations in our serving engine — lower latency and better batching. If you bring your own runtime in Private, we provide integration patterns.
[05:22] Eliot: Any customers that migrated off OpenAI and saw parity issues?
[05:26] Priya: Yes — some saw small differences due to tokenization and sampling randomness. Those were resolved by aligning tokenizers, using the same seed for eval, or selecting compatible model weights. We document the divergence and mitigation steps.
[05:40] Jordan: Ok let's talk security checklist items quickly — SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, data residency. Samir, any other must-haves?
[05:48] Samir: We need private subnets, restricted egress, and a way to rotate keys. Also pen-test reports would help.
[05:54] Priya: We include key rotation patterns and can require HSM-backed KMS for Private. Pen-test and SOC2 will be shared.
[06:00] Marta: Who will own the pilot on Redwood side?
[06:04] Jordan: I'll be your AE and Priya will run the tech lead. We'll set up a weekly sync.
[06:10] Sam (Product): Anything else on integration timeline? We're aiming for a Q2 pilot.
[06:15] Jordan: Sounds aligned. We'll send a proposed timeline with milestones.
[06:20] Eliot: One more technical — latency p95 is sensitive to batching. Can you tune batching for lower latency?
[06:26] Priya: Yes. We provide batching knobs and a cost/latency tradeoff dashboard in Redwood Console. We can pin SLOs per route and disable aggressive batching for hotspot routes.
[06:38] Marta: Great. For eval metrics, can you support clinical accuracy metrics we run?
[06:42] Priya: Absolutely — we'll ingest your scoring harness and produce regression alerts if quality drops.
[06:48] Jordan: Next steps recap: I'll send pricing, SOC2/pen test and SSO docs; Priya will share benchmark template and runbook; Eliot will share prompt set and traffic profile; schedule pilot kickoff late April.
[07:02] Marta: Works for us. Thanks.
[07:05] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with links — deck + benchmark sheet.
[07:10] (call ends)
